title: Feasibility analysis of the use of a telemonitoring platform for patients with respiratory infections
summary: Respiratory infections and pneumonia often lead to long hospital stays. Outpatient care via a telemonitoring platform can shorten hospital stays and increase patient satisfaction. After patients are discharged from inpatient treatment, self-measured vital signs and quality of life parameters are forwarded to the clinic's treatment team via a telemonitoring platform for a period of two weeks.

interventions.name:
Patients with respiratory infections and pneumonia are discharged early from inpatient treatment to outpatient care using a telemonitoring platform.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Written consent form signed by the study participant
2. Confirmation of a respiratory tract infection (infiltrate on chest X-ray or chest CT scan, confirmation of a respiratory tract infection in virological or microbiological tests)
3. Oxygen saturation while breathing ambient air in the range of at least 92% to 94% or use of oxygen therapy (e.g., oxygen concentrator) to achieve an oxygen saturation of at least 92% to 94%
Exclusion criteria:
1. No signed consent form from the study participant
2. Patients unable to give consent
3. No signs of a respiratory tract infection (no evidence of infiltrates on chest X-ray or chest CT scan, no confirmation of a respiratory tract infection in virological or microbiological tests)
4. Oxygen saturation below 92% while breathing ambient air or when using oxygen therapy (e.g., oxygen concentrator)
